title_options: Ollama Returns an Empty Response? Check the Token Limit
Ollama Returns HTTP 200 With No Tool Call: Read done_reason=length
Empty tool_calls From Ollama: Diagnose the Token Cap, Not the Model
presentation.title_rationale: The reader problem is an agent loop that receives HTTP 200, empty content and no tool_calls and cannot tell a truncated call from a model that declined to act. The selected title frontloads the product (Ollama) and the observable symptom (an empty response), states one supported benefit (checking the token limit separates a capped-and-dropped call from a finished turn) and names no fix, number, version or benchmark. The imperative is inspection, not 'raise the cap', which the body's own negative result and the cover caveat make explicit; the alternative phrasings were rejected because they push the field name done_reason=length into the headline, which is jargon the reader has not met yet.
presentation.visual_purpose: The cover is a conceptual three-step checklist for the state described in the article: the response is HTTP 200 with empty content, so inspect the stop reason, then the token usage, and do not assume a larger cap repairs it. It is grounded only in the article's measured negative result (0 complete calls across caps 8-64, one at 96) and shows no axis, percentage or boundary value; it labels itself a conceptual checklist rather than measurement data, so its scope is exactly the diagnostic ordering, not an inference about how many tokens any model needs.
